image_description: A close-up, cropped view of a large marine mammal's back and side at the water surface. The skin is dark grey with mottled lighter patches, consistent with barnacle encrustation. The body appears robust and spindle-shaped. No head, flippers, or tail are visible in this tight frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely outside the frame; only the mid-section of the body is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey coloration and white speckling indicative of barnacles/cyamids.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal ridge visible in the image lacks a true fin and shows the subtle undulations/knuckles typical of a grey whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The curvature and mass of the visible body section suggest a large, robust, spindle-shaped anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
